newsitem.title: USA: Gore favors tougher action in Alomar spitting case.
newsitem.headline: Gore favors tougher action in Alomar spitting case.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore, advocating civility in American society in a campaign debate, on Wednesday stepped into the controversy over baseball star Roberto Alomar, saying he should have been punished immediately for spitting at an umpire.

"I think he should have been severely disciplined, suspended perhaps, immediately. I don't understand why that action was not taken," Gore said during a televised debate with Republican vice-presidential candidate Jack Kemp.

The Baltimore Orioles second baseman was given a five-game suspension, to take effect at the start of the next regular season, for spitting in the face of an an umpire after contesting a decision during a regular season game against the Toronto Blue Jays on Sept. 27.
Many commentators, outraged at the example set by Alomar in the televised incident, said the player should have faced instant suspension, which would have kept him out of the play-off games.
Major league umpires threatened to strike the playoffs if Alomar played, but they dropped that threat when a court told them to go to work.
